findings.evidence: Voice cards are loaded after ensure_facts awaits while chapters come from earlier discovery; TOCTOU only hurts if cards/manuscript change mid-run.
findings.message: ghostreader/companion/pipeline.py:412-415 — Inconsistent filesystem snapshot. Authors are hurt: voice-card rows can compare manuscript text with cards reread after awaits, attributing findings to a card revision that did not match the manuscript snapshot.

findings.evidence: update_progress_after_run at 626-632 already passes max_chapter_on_disk=disk_max into _clamp_last, so the cursor is clamped on the same run, not left above disk for the next run.
findings.message: ghostreader/companion/pipeline.py:620-630 — Progress cursor exceeds disk state. Companion operators are hurt: the cursor can advance beyond chapters on disk, then be clamped back on the next run, causing repeated processing and spurious progress warnings.

findings.evidence: analyze_register_findings does scan all chapters then slice to cap, but that is CPU waste only; no wrong rows or dropped correctness on the default path.
findings.message: ghostreader/report/register_export.py:38-48 — Unbounded work before cap. Analyze users are hurt: all chapters are detected, materialized, and sorted even though the caller keeps at most 15 rows, wasting CPU on discarded findings.

findings.evidence: pyproject.toml requires-python >=3.12, so datetime.UTC (3.11+) is supported; companion import does not break on the supported runtime.
findings.message: ghostreader/companion/progress.py:17 — Importing datetime.UTC breaks companion startup on Python versions below 3.11, instead of retaining the previously compatible UTC form.

findings.evidence: VOICE_CARD_FINDINGS_CAP is enforced in detect_voice_card_issues (max_entries slice) and again in companion_voice_card_to_dicts; constants module is not required to enforce.
findings.message: ghostreader/companion/voice_card_constants.py:10–11 — The declared finding cap has no enforcement point here. Users may see different machine and companion finding counts, and per-chapter row budgets may be exceeded.

findings.evidence: COMMON_ENGLISH (uncommon thrash pre-filter) and READER_EXEMPT_WORDS (common-word skip) are complementary detectors by design, not conflicting exemptions for the same finding kind.
findings.message: ghostreader/analyzers/thrash_detector.py:45 — Conflicting word exemptions. Authors can see the same word treated as harmless by one thrash detector and reported by another, making findings inconsistent.

findings.evidence: _companion_prose_typesafe_state does set register_data/voice_card_data to None, but no in-repo TypeSafe schema proof of rejection or literal 'None' prompt rendering.
findings.message: ghostreader/companion/craft.py:122–128 — State schema compatibility. Typesafe users may have requests rejected if the client disallows the added keys or null values, or receive literal “None” as prompt context.

findings.evidence: Same cap/priority starvation as c1aaf755373a65d9: high-count cross_chapter still loses to higher-priority kinds at equal severity under the shared sort.
findings.message: ghostreader/report/thrash_export.py:88 — Severe cross-chapter misses. Authors searching for repeated invented nouns can receive no cross_chapter row for high-count lemmas whose within-scene rank is low.

findings.evidence: voice_card_detector imports and uses these cue/cap/title constants; wiring is live, so the unwired-detector claim is factually wrong.
findings.message: ghostreader/companion/voice_card_constants.py:1–98 — Constants without a wired detector. Users may be prompted for voice-card judgments without supplied cards or heuristic rows, leading to invented voice-mismatch concerns.

findings.evidence: _is_title_token exact-matches TITLE_SKIP_TOKENS on whole tokens; 'Drake'/'Draper' are not skipped, so substring title corruption of those names does not occur.
findings.message: ghostreader/companion/voice_card_constants.py:20–40 — Substring title matching can corrupt names such as “Drake” or “Draper”; users may lose or misattribute dialogue for those characters.

findings.evidence: Register/voice dims default on with companion_*_watch, but prompts tell the model to judge from manuscript and treat heuristic rows as optional bias, not require rows.
findings.message: ghostreader/companion/craft.py:160–168 — Unprompted register judgments. Users without register or voice-card data may receive fabricated craft findings because these dimensions are enabled by default and the prompt asks for judgments without supporting rows.

findings.evidence: Same datetime.UTC import claim as 936eb6add0347145; still false under requires-python >=3.12.
findings.message: ghostreader/companion/progress.py:8 — Unsupported datetime import. Users on Python 3.10 or earlier cannot import the companion package because datetime.UTC is unavailable.

findings.evidence: register_detector only constructs kinds unearned_jargon and initiation_budget; the else→unearned_jargon coercion is dead defensive code, not a leak of companion-only kinds into analyze.
findings.message: ghostreader/companion/register.py:25 — Kind coercion. Consumers of register findings are hurt: unsupported kinds are exported as `unearned_jargon`, so companion-only rows can leak into analyze exports mislabeled as jargon.

findings.evidence: Prompt forbids inventing a register_findings kind while machine register_findings are a separate brief field; no concrete path shown that merges them indistinguishably.
findings.message: ghostreader/companion/craft.py:60–80 — The prompt forbids register finding kinds while the report exposes machine register rows. Users may receive model-invented register findings indistinguishable from heuristic results.

findings.evidence: max_chapter_on_disk is a simple glob max with no lock; concurrent truncate during discover is a hypothetical race, not a default single-operator path.
findings.message: ghostreader/companion/discovery.py:48–50 — The disk maximum can be stale during a concurrent truncate; callers may unnecessarily re-analyze the newest chapter and duplicate findings.

findings.evidence: clamp_progress_to_disk is called from pipeline.py:278 before compute_order_warnings, and update_progress_after_run also clamps via _clamp_last.
findings.message: ghostreader/companion/progress.py:88–104 — The new clamp is not called by the shown callers. After a story is restored to an earlier chapter, users can retain an overstated cursor and receive false regression or skip warnings.

findings.evidence: update_progress_after_run applies the same _clamp_last persist as clamp_progress_to_disk (finding 34bcc41bc96e3f9a); same cursor-lowering defect, not a separate concurrent-race bug in pipeline's snapshotted disk_max.
findings.message: ghostreader/companion/progress.py:155–180 — A concurrent truncate can lower persisted progress after a run, causing chapters 5–9 to be re-analyzed and duplicate findings to be emitted.

findings.evidence: thrash_findings is a documented additive ReportOutput/JSON field (ANALYZE_HOOK); exposing machine rows is the contract, not an accidental schema break.
findings.message: ghostreader/report/__init__.py:75 — Public schema exposure. End users or strict report consumers may receive the machine-only thrash rows or reject the payload because of the added field.

findings.evidence: detect_voice_card_issues only emits card_mismatch and card_collapse; unknown-kind→card_mismatch coercion never relabels real detector rows on the product path.
findings.message: ghostreader/companion/voice_card.py:31-32 — Unknown kind coercion. Companion brief consumers are hurt: unsupported detector rows pass the kind filter as `card_mismatch`, so users receive rows mislabeled as a mismatch.

findings.evidence: Line 66 does int(ch.get("chapter_number") or 0), but product Chapter.chapter_number is always int via loaders/chapters_to_dicts, so nonnumeric-ID export loss is not on the default path.
findings.message: ghostreader/report/thrash_export.py:49 — Invalid chapter identifier handling. Users supplying otherwise usable chapter content with a nonnumeric identifier can lose the entire export to a conversion error.

findings.evidence: Helper defaults enabled=True by documented caller contract; sole product caller cli.py:382-400 sets thrash_enabled = analyze_thrash_watch and depth in {standard, deep}, so quick depth does not run scans.
findings.message: ghostreader/report/thrash_export.py:44 — Missing depth/watch enforcement. Users on quick depth can incur all detector scans if the caller does not gate the default-enabled export, despite the documented opt-in behavior.

findings.evidence: str(f.get('summary', ...)) would render 'None' if summary were null, but adapters/enrich keep summary as a non-null str on the TypeSafe path, so literal None is not a default-product failure.
findings.message: ghostreader/companion/craft.py:274 — Null note rendering. Users may see the literal text “None” when an enrichment summary is null, replacing the existing dimension note.

findings.evidence: pipeline skips craft under continuity_only and passes include_* from companion_*_watch; stock callers do not silently inherit extra dims against those flags.
findings.message: ghostreader/companion/craft.py:303–306 — Opt-out defaults. Callers expecting continuity-only or the stock five-dimension set may silently receive four extra dimensions, changing ratings and judgment counts.

findings.evidence: craft.py:300-306 is only run_companion_craft's parameter list; the body awaits one typesafe/LLM path with no shared store, lock, retry, or late-result budget to bound.
findings.message: ghostreader/companion/craft.py:300–306 — No shared result store, lock, retry, or budget is shown to bound late results; callers have no demonstrated protection against work finishing after they have moved on.

findings.evidence: ReportOutput already declares register_findings and thrash_findings and from_final_report accepts them; cli.py:391-400 construction cannot TypeError on those fields.
findings.message: ghostreader/cli.py:391-400 — Report model incompatibility. Analyze users are hurt if `ReportOutput` does not accept or expose these fields: report construction or JSON export fails with a `TypeError` or `AttributeError`.

findings.evidence: thrash_detector.py:247 is the COMMON_ENGLISH entry 'look', not Zipf omission; missing-lemma→not-uncommon lives at is_uncommon (KD-5) around lines 589-599.
findings.message: ghostreader/analyzers/thrash_detector.py:247 — Omitted Zipf entries are treated as common. Authors can miss uncommon-word thrash findings for words absent from the vendored score subset.

findings.evidence: Line 289 only sets initiation_budget span_end_word; _opening_window_text whitespace find reconstruction did not show a default-path truncation that leaves in-window terms unexamined.
findings.message: ghostreader/analyzers/register_detector.py:289 — Token-boundary miscount. Users can receive an initiation-budget count and excerpt that disagree with the first-N-words window, causing terms after the actual truncation point to go unexamined.
